reasons: The lake record is verified and identifies the case as United States v. Montoya de Hernandez in the U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1985-07-01.
The official citation, vendor-neutral cite, and listed parallel citations match the lake citation fields.

defect.evidence_quote: reasonably suspect that the traveler is smuggling contraband in her alimentary canal
defect.problem: The holding field is truncated at the operative condition. The opinion supports the rule only when officers have reasonable or articulable suspicion and the detention lasts only as reasonably necessary to verify or dispel that suspicion.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the holding with a complete formulation: a nonroutine border detention of a suspected alimentary-canal smuggler is justified at inception when agents reasonably suspect, based on all facts, that the traveler is smuggling contraband in her alimentary canal, and detention for the time reasonably necessary to verify or dispel that suspicion is not unreasonable.

reasons: The opinion states the reasonable-suspicion standard for detention at inception.
The opinion separately states that detention for the period necessary to verify or dispel the suspicion was not unreasonable.
The page holding ends with an ellipsis after 'customs officers have', omitting the required suspicion standard and duration limitation.
residual_risks: The lake pinpoints are marked quote_fidelity mismatch and slip-only, but no separate quote_fidelity or pincite assertion appears in the inventory.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid 'prolonged detention is reasonable' standing alone; tie reasonableness to reasonable suspicion plus the time reasonably necessary to verify or dispel it.

reasons: The opinion is a border-search case and says the Court had not previously decided the suspicion level for an incoming traveler seizure beyond a routine border search.
The opinion announces the reasonable-suspicion standard for alimentary-canal smuggling detentions at the border, supporting a refinement role.
The lake progeny metadata lists substantial citing-opinion and citation counts, supporting the 'Key' component of the role.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not define the page-role taxonomy, so this verifies the role only against the opinion and lake metadata.
